column1: # decoupled-scalar completion latency on sm_89 (CUDA-13 ptxas binary analysis + sm_89 GPU measurement)
# SCOREBOARD MECHANISM
# A decoupled scalar op does not deliver its result a fixed number of cycles after issue. It runs in a side
# pipe (SFU for the transcendentals/bit-ops, the MIO datapath for S2R/LDC, the FMA64 pipe for the 64-bit
# conversions) and arms one of the warp's six write scoreboards SB0..SB5. The result becomes visible only
# once that side pipe retires and clears the scoreboard. ptxas pairs the producer with its dependent
# consumer purely through that handshake: the producer's control word sets dst_wr_sb=n (bits 110-112); the
# consumer's control word carries a read-barrier wait on bit n of req_bit_set (bits 116-121) and stalls at
# the warp scheduler until SBn clears. The producer's own usched field (bits 105-109) is only its issue
# throughput, never the completion latency -- the completion time is whatever the side pipe takes, surfaced
# to the compiler solely as the scoreboard wait. So the per-op latency is the producer's pipe completion
# time, not a fixed result band.
# Which scoreboard a given producer arms is whichever of SB0..SB5 is free at that point (SB0 by default; a
# probe whose input setup already used SB0 makes the next producer arm SB1, etc.). The pairing is invariant:
# producer sets SBk -> the consumer that reads its result waits SBk.
# COUPLED EXCEPTIONS (no scoreboard)
# Two ops the fixed-band model treated as decoupled are emitted COUPLED on sm_89: CS2R (clock read) and the
# 32-bit integer->float conversion (lowered to I2FP). They arm no write scoreboard; ptxas resolves their RAW
# with a fixed issue stall instead, so a dependent use needs no scoreboard wait. The decoupled I2F path is
# the 64-bit conversion (I2F.F64.S64, FMA64 pipe); the 32-bit form is the coupled I2FP.
# METHOD
#  source_model        the prior heuristic fixed result band (cycles) the scalar model assigned.
#  sets_scoreboard     SBn the producer arms in ptxas -arch sm_89 output (-coupled if it arms none).
#  ptxas_emitted_wait  how ptxas makes a dependent consumer wait: "wait SBn" (scoreboard read-barrier) for a
#                      decoupled producer, or "coupled/stall=N" (no scoreboard; fixed issue stall) otherwise.
#  gpu_measured_latency  sm_89 GPU clock-delta: one producer->consumer pair bracketed by two SR_CLOCKLO reads
#                      (S2UR then CS2R), single warp of 32 lanes, with the scoreboard wait intact; the
#                      per-lane (clock_after - clock_before) minus the back-to-back clock-read overhead
#                      (36 cyc, measured empty-body). This is the producer's completion latency as seen by a
#                      dependent use: producer pipe completion + the dependent op's own issue. The coupled
#                      floor (a coupled producer feeding the same consumer) is 11 cyc -- the CS2R/I2FP rows
#                      pin it directly -- so the pure scoreboard premium is gpu_measured_latency - 11 for the
#                      same-consumer (int/fp) ops. Deterministic across repeated launches.
# All cycle figures are sm_89 (RTX Ada, compute capability 8.9), CUDA 13.1 ptxas/nvdisasm. The 64-bit
# conversions (F2F.F64.F32, I2F.F64.S64) feed an FP64 consumer (DADD), which inflates their measured number
# by the FP64 add latency. LDC's number is an uncached indirect constant-bank fetch (cold const cache); a
# cache-resident LDC resolves far faster (the source band's 30 is the warm-hit figure).
# Reproduce: probe_decoupled_scalar.py (no args -> ptxas-emitted pairings; --gpu -> the clock-delta sweep).
